ImportExpenses.title: Import expenses
ImportExpenses.description: Add expenses to this group from a file made with Export to JSON or Export to CSV.
ImportExpenses.body: Choose a file exported from Spliit. It’s checked first, and you’ll see what it contains before anything is added.
ImportExpenses.requirements: Everyone in the file must already be a participant of this group, with the same name, and the group must use the same currency.
ImportExpenses.formats: JSON keeps everything. CSV doesn’t record who paid when the payer isn’t part of the split, which is often the case for reimbursements: those can only be imported from JSON.

Issues.fileTooLarge: The file is too large ({size}). The limit is {max}.
Issues.invalidJson: The file looks like JSON but can’t be read. It may be damaged or incomplete.
Issues.jsonStructure: This JSON file isn’t a Spliit export: “{field}” is missing or has the wrong type.
Issues.csvSyntax: a quoted value is never closed, so the file can’t be read from here on.
Issues.csvHeader: This isn’t a Spliit CSV export. Its first row must have the columns {expected}, then one column per person.
Issues.noExpenses: The file doesn’t contain any expenses.
Issues.tooManyExpenses: The file has {count} expenses, but at most {max} can be imported at once. Split it into smaller files.
Issues.currencyMismatch: The file’s amounts are in {file}, but this group uses {group}. Expenses can only be imported into a group with the same currency.
Issues.unknownParticipants: These people in the file aren’t participants of this group: {names}. Add them in the group settings, with the same names, then import again.
Issues.jsonExpenseStructure: “{field}” is missing or has the wrong type.
Issues.jsonUnknownParticipantId: it refers to a participant (“{id}”) that the file doesn’t list.
Issues.columnCount: it has {actual} values, but the first row has {expected} columns.
Issues.invalidDate: “{value}” isn’t a valid date. Use the YYYY-MM-DD format.
Issues.invalidAmount: “{value}” in {column} isn’t a valid amount. Use a plain number like 12.50: no currency sign, no thousands separator, and no more decimals than the currency has.
Issues.missingValue: the column for {column} is empty. Use 0 for someone who isn’t part of the expense.
Issues.invalidSplitMode: “{value}” isn’t a split mode. Use Evenly, Unevenly – By shares, Unevenly – By percentage or Unevenly – By amount.
Issues.invalidYesNo: “{value}” in {column} should be Yes or No.
Issues.invalidCurrencyCode: “{value}” isn’t a currency code, like EUR.
Issues.payerNotFound: no one in this row can be the payer.
Issues.multiplePayers: more than one person looks like the payer. In a Spliit CSV export, only the payer’s amount has the same sign as the cost.
Issues.ambiguousPayer: the CSV doesn’t say who paid, because the payer isn’t part of the split (often the case for a reimbursement). Import the JSON export instead: it records the payer.
Issues.sharesMismatch: the people’s amounts add up to {sum}, not to the cost of {amount}.
Issues.unevenSplit: the split mode is Evenly, but the amounts aren’t even.
Issues.duplicateParticipant: the same person is in the split more than once.

Reasons.amountSum: the amounts don’t add up to the expense amount.
Reasons.percentageSum: the percentages don’t add up to 100%.
